title: Ten Million Francs
subtitle: Never press others about personal matters. They always reveal themselves with time.

items.text: Ten Million Francs
Pawnshop

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Didn't expect to see you again so soon, Fleming.
From behind the thick glass wall of the counter, Drelome pokes out with a bemused look on his face.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Thought you just pulled off a big deal? Have you burned through all that money so soon?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Don't ask stupid questions, Drelome. You'll live longer.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: But of course. Your business is your own; only I wonder if you're willing to name a price on that pistol of yours now.
Fleming shoots him a look of cold disdain as he sets a plain wooden box on the counter.
A withered hand reaches across, opens it, then snaps it shut again.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: She is beautiful indeed. So, what sort of deal are you after?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Ten million. Cash.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Impossible.
He pushes the box back across the glass.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Damn it, you realize that right there is "The Merciful Maria"!

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: It may be, it may not be; all I can see is a "Greedy Fleming."

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: It has a fine story, bloody, dark; I may have a customer. But for ten million?

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: As I told you before, my offer was only ever going to drop.
Fleming slides the pistol box back across the counter again.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Nine.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Eight. And naturally you'll be signing all the relevant transfers.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... Deal!

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Voila, sign here. I'll have the money sent your way—minus a five percent fee, of course.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You slimy old drunk. After I strike it rich, I'll buy this whole block and put you out on the street.
He scrawls his name across the page.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: I will be looking forward to that day, monsieur.
Fleming turns, his step and demeanor a combination of excitement and anger.
Hotel Room
It's a plain, tired old inn, just across the street from the pawnshop.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Tennant leans against the window, idly spinning a revolver. Cobwebs glint faintly in the corner, waiting for some unlucky insect.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Fleming's been in that pawnshop for twenty minutes now.
You think he'll get ten million?
The cylinder snaps open, spins fast under her thumb, then clicks shut again—Empty.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I can hardly imagine Drelome being that generous, can you?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: The old fox might barely be able to walk without wobbling, but he's still sharp.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Little doubt he'll sniff out Fleming's desperation.
You think he'll get seven?
The cylinder spins again, stops. Still empty.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I doubt he'd part with it for less. We are talking about "The Merciful Maria."

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Our friend went to great lengths—from procuring those diamonds to fixing up that box—just to get her hands on it.
Heh ... so eight million?
The cylinder spins a third time with a faint whir, just as Fleming comes into view outside Tennant's window.
Tennant holds the cylinder still, a diamond bullet ready in its chamber.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: From the look on his face, I do believe you're right on the money.
Eight million is still a fine haul. Enough to buy a villa in Saint-Remèze, complete with a Second Empire stone fireplace and southern sunlight.
I can see it now. Fully electrified, ready for everything a modern life requires.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Money isn't the goal of this game of ours. Ten million is just the bottom line. The only way to prove the seeker's sincerity.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Say what you will about the man, he's crafty. I do believe he'll find a way to gather that final two million.
You should head back to your little lab. Odds are he's eager to get that money in your hands.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: No, I doubt that.
Oh?
Tennant watches as Fleming turns and disappears into the alley.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I said he was crafty, but note I didn't say wise.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I'm sure when he first laid eyes on those synthetic gemstones, he was giddy with delight.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: But now, the rush has worn off. He's pawned off his most prized possession, and now he's wandering Paris laden with cash.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: No, I believe he'll cool off first.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Then, because he is crafty, if not clever. I do believe he'll make an effort to hedge his bets. He might start digging into just who this "Brette Cosette" really is.
Oh, so you think Brette's about to be exposed. How will she handle it?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: With sincerity—always, sincerity is her greatest strength.
